newsitem.title: USA: Charges dropped against two cops in driver's death.
newsitem.headline: Charges dropped against two cops in driver's death.

text.p: Two white policemen accused of killing a black motorist will not face trial because they were unfairly singled out for charges, a judge ruled Tuesday.
At a hearing, Allegheny County Judge David Cashman dismissed charges of involuntary manslaughter against Brentwood Lt. Milton Mulholland and Baldwin Officer Michael Albert.
"That is his ruling. The opinion has been filed with the clerk of courts," a clerk in Cashman's chambers said.
In his ruling, Cashman also removed District Attorney Bob Colville and his staff from the case.
Colville, reached at his office, said he will appeal his removal as well as the dismissed charges. "I feel very comfortable that we will win," he said.

Mulholland and Albert had been charged in the October 12, 1995 death of Jonny Gammage, a 31-year-old black man who was a cousin and business partner of Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Ray Seals.

Their first trial ended in a mistrial last year when Allegheny County Coroner Cyril Wecht said on the witness stand that Albert should "explain his actions" the night of Gammage's death. A defendant is not required to testify at a trial.
Another officer who had been charged with involuntary manslaughter, Brentwood Patrolman John Vojtas, also went on trial last year and was acquitted in November.

The incident began when Mulholland pulled Gammage over early in the morning, for what he said was erratic driving. He said Gammage became violent after leaving his car as other officers were arriving to provide backup.

The officers testified in a coroner's inquest that they had to restrain Gammage by holding him face-down on the ground. The cause of death was listed as suffocation caused by compression to the neck and chest.
An autopsy report showed no signs of drugs or alcohol in Gammage's bloodstream, although marijuana had been found in the car he was driving, a Jaguar that belonged to Seals.
Three of the five officers involved in the incident were charged.
